clue.text: City diner hosting retirement of current medic

indicators.note: the diner takes in the other letters as a host takes in guests

parts.note: a caff is British slang for a cheap café or diner

indicators.note: retiring is going back, so the current and the medic are read backwards

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
DR is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A town eatery entertains a doctor as he steps back from practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardiff is the capital city of Wales.

clue.text: Record time inside, being so confined

indicators.note: the time goes within the record's letters

parts.note: a CD is a compact disc, a record
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A criminal on record does time behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record time' looks like a fastest-ever time; 'time inside' also suggests a prison term.
explanation.definitionFit: Caged means shut in or imprisoned, as an animal behind bars.

clue.text: Discharge rector replacing bishop as head of trust

indicators.note: the rector takes the bishop's place
the swap happens at the front of the word for trust

parts.note: to believe is to trust
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A church trust dismisses its rector and puts a bishop in charge instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve someone of a duty is to discharge or release them from it.

clue.text: Dope harvested from rainforest becomes most precious

indicators.note: harvested crops are taken out of the land, so letters are taken from within the word

explanation.surface: A drug gathered in the jungle turns out to be priceless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' suggests drugs; it is slang for information. The closing words only dress the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is informal for inside information, as in 'the latest dope'.

clue.text: Brew home beer, fitting at the moment

indicators.note: brewing stirs ingredients together, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Homebrewed beer suits us for now.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means temporarily, for the present, until things change.

clue.text: Physical border, which the sun doesn't cross

definitions.text: Physical border, which the sun doesn't cross

parts.words: Physical border, which the sun doesn't cross
parts.note: a boundary on the body marking where clothing kept sunlight off the skin

explanation.walkthrough: 'Physical border' suggests a frontier between countries; here physical means bodily.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the visible edge on skin between bronzed and untouched areas left by swimwear or straps.

clue.text: Hearing it, Jimmy, Graham and Benny might have risen again!

definitions.text: Hearing it, Jimmy, Graham and Benny might have risen again!

parts.words: Hearing it, Jimmy, Graham and Benny might have risen again!
parts.note: Jimmy, Graham and Benny Hill were famous Britons, all dead; the film's song says the hills are alive with this

explanation.walkthrough: Jimmy Hill was a football pundit, Graham Hill a racing driver, Benny Hill a comedian. The musical's opening line 'The hills are alive' would bring them back to life.
explanation.definitionFit: The title song of the Rodgers and Hammerstein musical opens 'The hills are alive with' this phrase.

clue.text: Canon's done exercising — it doesn't take long

indicators.note: exercising puts things through their paces, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: The cleric has finished his workout, which was very short.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanosecond is a billionth of a second, a vanishingly brief interval.

clue.text: List that is covering broadcast times

indicators.note: the abbreviation wraps around the other letters

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters of times are rearranged

explanation.surface: A schedule covering when programmes air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast times' reads as a TV schedule, but 'broadcast' is the anagram signal, and 'that is' is the Latin abbreviation i.e.
explanation.definitionFit: To itemise is to set out item by item, as in a detailed list.

clue.text: It finishes fast, getting new direction

parts.note: Easter ends Lent, the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: Something ends quickly and takes a different course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' reads as speedy but means a period of abstinence.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastern means towards or from the east, a compass direction.

clue.text: Feel cargo gets damaged by such wind

indicators.note: the cargo being damaged means these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A ship's freight is ruined in a storm, and you can sense it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gale-force wind is one strong enough to rank as a gale on the Beaufort scale.

clue.text: Spotted returning, carrying daughter's essentials

indicators.note: the reversed word holds the daughter inside it, as if carrying her
returning means the word for spotted is read backwards

parts.note: spotted means seen
D is the abbreviation for daughter, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone seen coming home bearing a girl's must-have items.
explanation.definitionFit: Needs are necessities, the things one cannot do without.

clue.text: One way to get slimmed down parliament

definitions.text: One way to get slimmed down
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a regime of controlled eating for weight loss
second meaning: a legislative assembly, as in Japan's or historically the Holy Roman Empire's

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests trimming the size of a parliament; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a weight-loss eating plan and the name of certain national legislative assemblies.

clue.text: County stores let rector inside

indicators.note: the rector is placed within the other letters

parts.note: stores are shops
to let a property is to hire it out

explanation.surface: Shops in the shire let a vicar take premises.
explanation.definitionFit: Shropshire is an English county on the Welsh border.

clue.text: Broke off engagement on Facebook? It wasn't meant to be!

definitions.meaning: first meaning, playful: as 'unfriended' removes a friend, this removes one's intended, a fiancé
second meaning: not done on purpose

explanation.walkthrough: An intended is a fiancé; by analogy with Facebook's 'unfriend', dropping one would leave them un-intended.
explanation.definitionFit: The ordinary sense is accidental, not planned or deliberate.

clue.text: One may be roasted from exercise with a fanatic

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
a nut is an enthusiast, as in a fitness nut

explanation.surface: Someone gets mocked for doing workouts alongside a zealot.
explanation.definitionFit: Peanuts are commonly dry-roasted and salted as a snack.

clue.text: Eccentric uncle working to find subatomic particle

indicators.note: an eccentric uncle is an odd one, so his letters are rearranged

parts.note: on means functioning or working

explanation.surface: A quirky relative busy in the lab discovers a tiny particle.
explanation.definitionFit: A nucleon is a proton or neutron, a constituent of an atomic nucleus.

clue.text: Not many screwed up? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: screwed up means messed up, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Asking whether only a few made mistakes, and hearing the reverse is true.
explanation.definitionFit: An antonym is a word of contrary meaning, as hot is to cold.

clue.text: Unfortunately, it's holding up better source of wool

indicators.note: the exclamation holds the other letters within it

parts.note: alas is said when things go unfortunately

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to cap is to better or outdo

explanation.surface: Sadly, the improved wool supply is being held up.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpacas are South American camelids farmed for their soft fleece.

clue.text: In two minds over a party — it requires quick turnaround

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first word above the rest

parts.note: torn means undecided between two options
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Undecided about a celebration that needs to be organised fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quick turnaround' sounds like a deadline, but describes rapid spinning.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violently rotating column of air, spinning very fast.

clue.text: In the middle of town, diners cursed the proprietors

indicators.note: the central pair of letters is taken from each of the three following words

explanation.surface: Restaurant customers in the town centre swore at the people who own the place.
explanation.definitionFit: Proprietors are those who own a business or property.

clue.text: Back up religious type suppressing a Gaelic language

indicators.note: in a down clue, the cleric sits on top of the language, holding it down

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a cleric
Erse is an old name for Scottish or Irish Gaelic

explanation.surface: A cleric supports efforts to stamp out a Celtic tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: To reverse a vehicle is to back it up.

clue.text: Will plot fail if it doesn't go off?

definitions.text: Will plot fail if it doesn't go off?

parts.words: Will plot fail if it doesn't go off?
parts.note: a plot here is a scheme to kill by post, which fails if the explosive device mailed fails to detonate

explanation.walkthrough: 'Will plot' reads like a story plot or a bequest; it is a murderous scheme, and 'go off' means explode.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an explosive device sent through the mail, meant to detonate when opened.

clue.text: Loose violin section repels composer

indicators.note: repelling drives back, so the concealed letters are read backwards
a section is a part cut from the words, so the letters lie within them

explanation.surface: A slack string section pushes away a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'section' finds SEVI across looSE VIolin, and 'repels' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Ives was a modernist American composer.

clue.text: Declare note is sounding sort of identical?

indicators.note: the note is within the word for declare

parts.note: to say is to declare

indicators.note: the note is spelled as it is pronounced

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Asking whether a musical note sounds just like another.
explanation.definitionFit: Samey is informal for monotonously alike, lacking variety.

clue.text: Denounce dad and mom's new beginnings

indicators.note: the beginnings of the words are their initial letters

explanation.surface: Condemning a father and mother's fresh starts.
explanation.definitionFit: To damn is to condemn or criticise severely.

clue.text: Tip for cooking tough vegetable

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter

parts.note: hard means tough

explanation.surface: Kitchen advice on how to prepare a stringy vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Chard is a leafy green beet grown for its leaves and stalks.

clue.text: It stores images showing popular pair of beastly males

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
two male animals side by side: a stag, the male deer, and a ram, the male sheep

explanation.surface: A photo-sharing app displays a well-liked picture of two male animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pair of beastly males' gives two animals: STAG then RAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Instagram is a social media app for sharing photographs.

clue.text: Prove setter perhaps can be best in class, eventually

definitions.text: can be best in class, eventually

parts.note: to show is to prove
a setter is a gun-dog breed, an example of a dog

explanation.surface: A crossword setter shows he can top the class in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the puzzle's compiler, but it is the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog bred and trained for competitions may win best in its class at a show.

clue.text: Prudent having American medical facility in food processing plant

indicators.note: the prudent word has the hospital unit inside it

parts.note: canny means shrewd or prudent
ER is the American emergency room

explanation.surface: A careful firm with an on-site US clinic runs a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannery is a factory where food is sealed in tins.
